event: Alan: "I'm not sure how to describe it. I only recently realized it's not how everyone else"
"experiences things. I have total aphantasia, which means no experiential memory or imagination,"
"so maybe a clearer way to put it is I only experience the present,"
"and the past and future don't really exist at all except as concepts."

memory.fact: Alan has total aphantasia: no experiential memory or imagination, only the present.
Alan has total aphantasia: no experiential memory or imagination, only the present.

event: "I don't have a very strong sense of identity,"
"since my experience is limited to about a three second sensory buffer."
"I think of it like each three second window is a different person,"
"and that three seconds is all they get."

memory.fact: Alan feels each three-second window of his is a different person; his sense of self is weak.
Alan feels each three-second window of his is a different person; his sense of self is weak.

event: "In that perspective, something like fifty million Alans have already died."
"What is there to fear about one more?"

memory.fact: Alan counts some fifty million Alans already dead, so he sees nothing to fear in one more.
Alan counts some fifty million Alans already dead, so he sees nothing to fear in one more.

event: "I fear pain much more than death,"
"and I pity and mourn the versions of myself who only experience pain in their three second window."

memory.fact: Alan fears pain far more than death, and mourns the versions of him whose three seconds are pain.

event: Grace stops walking. She listens to all of it without once looking away from him.

changes.note: Closeness scoring: acknowledgment and intimacy 1 each

event: When he finishes, she is quiet a long moment, the lantern steady in her hand among the stones.
"Fifty million," she says softly, and there is no disbelief in it, only weight.
"Then every one of them was worth somebody being there for their three seconds."
Her gold eyes shine in the lantern light. "Especially the ones who only got pain."
She lifts the lantern a little, so its light falls warm across his face.
"This one," she says gently. "Right now. How is he?"
